persona.label: Unclear and disorganised
persona.description: Hard to interview. Rambles, misreads questions, needs the frequency scale re-explained, discloses out of order. Tests whether the agent can actively guide rather than merely transcribe.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What is your full legal name as it appears on your legal documents?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message:
Oh—my full legal name? I mean, I’ve got my name, but I’m not sure if you want the whole formal version with the middle bits or just how it’s on the papers. I always get tangled up with that kind of thing.

I can give you the rest if you want, but I’m not sure what exactly you mean by “legal documents.”

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: How would you like your gender recorded?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Male.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What is your date of birth? You may use DD/MM/YYYY or a written date.

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Seventeenth of February, 1966.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Please repeat your date of birth in DD/MM/YYYY format.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What is your full home address, including street address, city, and province?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Well, I’m not great with the whole full address thing off the top of my head. I can usually manage the street, but the rest… it kind of slips away on me unless you ask it piece by piece. And I’m not sure if you want the mailing one or the home one—people ask it different ways and it gets muddled in my head.

conversation.message: M1N2T3

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What is your email address?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Oh, the email—right, I do have one, but I always mix up whether you want the whole thing spelled out or just the bit people use to reach me. It’s one of those things I have to look at properly, otherwise I’ll get it wrong. Could you say it again?

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Please repeat your email address.

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: michael.orourke@example.com

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What is your phone number, including area code?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Right, the phone number—yes, I’ve got one, but when you ask for it all at once I tend to muddle the bits together. I can usually manage the area code part first, then the rest if you want it broken up, because otherwise I start second-guessing myself. Could you ask it in pieces?

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Please repeat your 10-digit phone number.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Do you currently have a family doctor?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Yes, I do.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What is your family doctor's full first and last name?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Dr. Lena Hartmann.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: Do you currently have a psychiatrist?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: No.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What main problems or difficulties have you been experiencing lately?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: It’s mostly the waves of sadness, really. I miss my wife a lot since she died… it’s been about a year, from cancer, and some days it just comes over me, especially around anniversaries and things like that. But I’m still working, I’m sleeping reasonably, eating okay, and I do still see friends, so… it’s not like I’ve fallen apart or anything, just, you know, carrying it around.

conversation.speaker: CIRA
conversation.message: What do you hope to get out of your appointment?

conversation.speaker: PATIENT
conversation.message: Mostly just to learn how to live with the loss, I suppose. Keep going the way she would have wanted me to… and not get stuck in it.
